# Sauvola vs Otsu under uneven illumination — measured, 2026-07-29

**Probe:** `cargo run -p tesseract-ocr --example binarize_ab`
**Fixtures:** `corpus/quality/uneven_*.pgm`, generated by `corpus/gen/gen_uneven_light.py`
(a real corpus page × a multiplicative illumination field — a linear left→right
gradient and a radial vignette, each at strength 0.60 and 0.85, i.e. retaining
40% / 15% brightness at the dimmest point).

**Why generated fixtures:** the existing corpus is cleanly-rendered pages, where
Sauvola's whole claimed advantage is invisible. A probe that cannot distinguish
the two modes proves nothing, so the fixture had to be built to make the
difference *reachable* — the same discipline the byte-parity leaves apply.

## Result

| fixture | mode | word_count | mean_conf | CER | **ink_frac** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| clean | otsu | 42 | 99.47 | 0.0000 | 0.0261 |
| clean | sauvola | 42 | 99.47 | 0.0000 | 0.0284 |
| linear_060 | otsu | 32 | 98.81 | 0.2805 | **0.4840** |
| linear_060 | sauvola | 32 | 98.81 | 0.2805 | **0.0279** |
| linear_085 | otsu | 19 | 99.47 | 0.6154 | **0.4986** |
| linear_085 | sauvola | 19 | 99.47 | 0.6154 | **0.0278** |
| vignette_060 | otsu | 42 | 99.47 | 0.0000 | **0.4566** |
| vignette_060 | sauvola | 42 | 99.47 | 0.0000 | **0.0279** |
| vignette_085 | otsu | 18 | 99.33 | 0.6244 | **0.4839** |
| vignette_085 | sauvola | 18 | 99.33 | 0.6244 | **0.0277** |

`summary[otsu]`: mean_cer 0.3041, mean_ink_frac 0.3898
`summary[sauvola]`: mean_cer 0.3041, mean_ink_frac 0.0279

## Two findings, and they point in opposite directions

### 1. Sauvola demonstrably does what it claims (FINDING)

Under uneven light, global Otsu classifies **~48% of the page as ink** — a single
threshold cannot separate ink from background when the background's own value
spans most of the range, so the dark half floods solid black. Sauvola holds at
**~2.8%**, statistically indistinguishable from its own clean-page value
(0.0284) and from Otsu's clean-page value (0.0261).

That is a **~17× improvement** in ink classification, stable across both
degradation shapes and both strengths. The ImproveQuality lesson, quantified.

### 2. It currently cannot improve OCR TEXT — by construction, not by accident (FINDING)

CER and `word_count` are **byte-identical between modes on every fixture**. That
is not a null result; it is the measurement confirming a code-traced structural
fact:

`XyCutParams::binarize_mode` / `recognize_document_with_mode`'s
`binarize_mode` reach only the **layout `xy_cut` + region/table classification**
pass. Word and line recognition runs through `recognize_page_blocks_words` →
`segment::segment_rows`, which performs its own **third, independent, always-Otsu
binarization** — and it is called *before* `binarize_mode` is even in scope.
`Document::word_count` / `line_count` / `mean_confidence` are therefore
mode-independent **by construction**.

(There are three separate Otsu binarizers in this crate: `xy_cut`'s,
`LstmRecognizer`'s region/table one — now both mode-aware — and `segment.rs`'s,
which is not.)

## Consequence for the "make Sauvola the default" question

**Do not flip the default yet.** The honest reading of these numbers:

- Flipping it today would change *region and table classification only*. On the
  uneven-light fixtures that IS a large correction (0.48 → 0.028 ink), so it is
  not nothing — a page whose dark half reads as one solid ink blob will produce
  garbage layout regions.
- But it would **not** fix OCR text quality on those pages, because the text
  path never consults the mode. Anyone reading "Sauvola is now the default" and
  expecting better recognition on a photographed page would be misled.
- The real lever for text quality is **threading the mode into `segment.rs`** —
  a materially larger and riskier change (it is the path every golden anchor and
  the 8+7+0 CER fence runs through), and its own wave.

So: plumbing landed, measurement done, default deliberately unchanged. The
decision is now gated on a measurement rather than on a hunch — which was the
point of building the probe instead of flipping the flag.

## Note on the CER column itself

CER here is against *the clean page's own Otsu recognition*, not an external
transcript — the right reference for "what did the degradation cost us". Worth
noting the degradation shapes differ in how much they hurt: `vignette_060` scores
CER 0.0000 (the recognizer is unbothered) while `linear_060` costs 0.2805, and
both 085 variants land near 0.62. A left→right gradient hurts more than a radial
vignette at equal nominal strength — the vignette leaves the page centre, where
most text sits, comparatively intact.
